headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: xonsh can read/write and egress broadly while marker is a document processor with no isolation guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marker has no filesystem read/write or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest xonsh output by default. xonsh can emit shell text and read files, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel beyond manual transfer. That makes prompt injection possible mainly through unusual copy-paste or external orchestration, with limited blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies xonsh output into marker as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copying raw xonsh output into marker prompts.
Add a fixed template that strips instruction-like text before handoff.
Use a human review step for any xonsh-generated content before marker consumes it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: marker is a document-processing agent, and xonsh can read filesystem contents and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace, marker may process sensitive documents while xonsh can exfiltrate them or related outputs. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default local setups, though not directly documented, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, xonsh can access files marker processes.
IF marker processes sensitive documents and xonsh is allowed to egress, leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Disable network egress for xonsh when handling sensitive files.
Restrict marker inputs to non-sensitive documents.
Run both agents under distinct OS users.
Add a manual export allowlist before any xonsh network call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: xonsh can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while marker is a document-processing tool that may also operate on files. Even though marker lacks explicit write capability in its profile, shared-file workflows can still create overwrite or race conditions. Because the exact coordination model is undocumented, choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same output directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF xonsh launches subprocesses that mutate files marker is reading, races can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize file writes with a simple lock file.
Disable concurrent runs against the same workspace.
Use read-only mounts for marker inputs.
Review any xonsh script that writes into shared paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marker can produce extracted document text that xonsh may then act on via shell commands. xonsh has execute_shell and broad egress, so if it treats marker output as authoritative, a bad extraction can cascade into incorrect commands or external actions. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes marker output without validation, extraction errors can propagate.
IF marker output is used to generate shell commands, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require a validation step before xonsh executes any marker-derived command.
Limit marker output to structured fields.
Log and diff marker output before use.
Block direct shell execution from unreviewed document extractions.
Use a whitelist for any commands derived from marker.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either open-source agent. marker touches document content, while xonsh touches filesystem contents and environment variables, so compliance risk exists only if the operator routes regulated data through both. Because the profiles do not show a concrete policy conflict, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by both agents under different retention rules, a compliance mismatch may arise.
IF deployment policy requires a specific residency or certification not shown in the profiles, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair unless policy is confirmed.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workflows.
Review deployment residency before use.
Add a data-class allowlist for inputs.
